page0.text:
...
No, this is important.
It's my decision, so I shouldn't push it onto someone else. It's only right that I be the one to tell Sakura.

page1.text:
Just as I make up my mind,
the doorbell rings with perfect timing.
"I'm coming in!"
It's Sakura's voice.
I'll ask Sakura right away. It's faster this way.

page2.text:
"Ah, Senpai. Thanks for having me over. Are you making dinner now?"
"Yeah, just starting. I can handle it on my own, so make yourself at home. If you would, could you keep Fuji-nee busy while you're at it? She's being a sore loser after Saber beat her at kendo, so cheer her up with a card game or something."

page3.text:
"That's mean, Senpai. Ms. Fujimura had a rough day, you know."
"Ahh, she did mention that...then play shogi with her, instead."

page4.text:
"Shogi? Okay, she's very confident at that.
I think it'll be just right if I give her a handicap and play without rooks."

page5.text:
Sakura's in a good mood.
The swelling on her face is gone, and there's no sign of the dark bruise from this morning.
Okay, now would be a good time to bring it up.

page6.text:
"So, Sakura. I know this is sudden, but you should stay over starting tonight."
"Huh? Stay over...?"
"You shouldn't go back to the Matou house for the time being. As for how long...let's try to make it a week. Oh, and I already got Fuji-nee's permission."

page7.text:
"..."
Sakura's expression stiffens.
She gazes back at me like she's scrutinizing my heart rather than my face.

page8.text: "I know I'm asking a lot. But still, I really want you to stay over. No matter how badly you might think of me, please live here for now."

page9.text:
...
Sakura doesn't answer.
She just keeps watching me, and I notice she slightly bites her lip.
"...Why?"
Finally, she asks me in a very quiet voice.

page10.text:
"..."
I can't give her a reason.
On my life's honor, I can't tell her it's because Shinji is a Master, but anything else would be a lie.
Everyone has secrets.
I'm a guy, so there's plenty of stuff I don't say to Sakura and Fuji-nee.

page11.text:
...No matter how precious someone is to you, there are some things you can't tell them.
That's all the more reason I can't lie to her.
If Sakura is my precious family, then I'd rather not tell her anything that's untrue.

page12.text:
"..."
The atmosphere between us chills.
Silence falls over us, and it seems to stretch on forever. Sakura awkwardly breaks eye contact.
I desperately rack my stupid brain for a response.

page13.text:
"Do I have to tell you why?"
She doesn't answer.
But her eyes seem to show concern for me, rather than herself.
"...Is it because you're worried about me?"
She states it outright.

page14.text:
"Yeah. I'm worried, so it would make me feel a lot better if you'd stay over."
Her long, dark hair sways.
Sakura nods at my inadequate answer,
and answers not with words, but a smile.
